chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:
I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the ring being worn in the right hand, so he said: 'If you wish, [wear it] in the right hand, and if you wish, [wear it] in the left hand.'
ai.seo_question: Where should a ring be worn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ali ibn Ja'far queries Imam Musa al-Kadhim regarding the permissibility of wearing a ring on the right hand, to which the Imam grants flexibility, allowing it on either hand. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that such adornments are permissible acts of *mustahabb* (recommended) practice rather than obligatory acts of worship, thereby distinguishing them from ritual items like the *khitam* of the Prophet. The narration underscores the practical leniency in personal adornment within the Imami tradition, provided it does not involve extravagance or arrogance.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said,

‘I asked my brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> about the ring to be worn in the right hand. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to, wear it in the right hand, and if you so desire to, in the left’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Ja‘far who has said the following: “I once asked my brother, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the ring; if it is worn on the right hand. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can wear it on the right or left, as you wish.’”
